execution.description: Built G6 for graph-only Level 4 and tested whether a graph lowered for one case and batched by Carbon's vmap trains like the native batched model, for battery's Level 0 MLP (classic loop) and DeepONet (training.train).

expected: A per-case graph batched by vmap is equivalent to the native batched model, as its forward pass is (Phase 0: forward outputs bit-identical on CPU), so the interface could fix one case and let Carbon batch.
observed: Forward passes matched bit for bit, but training did not for every family. The classic MLP trained bit-identically through vmap. DeepONet did not: same final loss to print precision, different parameter digest, because vmap changes the order in which gradients accumulate across the batch. Bit-identity in the forward pass does not carry to training.
keep: Lower a Level 4 graph at the recipe's own training batch and pin that batch at G4; train at it; pad inference into blocks of it, which keeps every case's result the declared graph's.
Test equivalence on training (parameter digests after the full step count), never only on the forward pass.
change: Any interface that fixes one case per graph needs its own R1 training evidence per family before it is used.
Run the same training-equivalence check on the GPU lane (the A40 R1 leg) before any Level 4 claim beyond CPU.
